hints: Look closely at the two ends of the molecules, what is the big structural change when lycopene becomes beta-carotene?
Count the total unsaturation in each molecule, remembering that each C=C double bond and each ring counts as one unit of unsaturation.
Compare the number of double bonds lost with the number of rings gained to decide if hydrogen atoms must be added or removed.
walkthrough:
**Spot the structural difference**

Look side by side and you will see the long middle chain is identical. The change is only at the two ends. Lycopene has open chain ends, while beta-carotene has those ends folded into two six-membered rings.

This is a cyclisation reaction, not addition or removal of side groups.

**Use unsaturation to track hydrogen**

For hydrocarbons, hydrogen count is controlled by the degree of unsaturation. Each double bond and each ring reduces the hydrogen count by 2 compared to the alkane.

$$\text{degree of unsaturation} = \text{number of } \pi \text{ bonds} + \text{number of rings}$$

**Count double bonds and rings**

Lycopene has 13 C=C double bonds and 0 rings, so total unsaturation = 13. Beta-carotene has 11 C=C bonds in the chain plus 1 C=C in each ring, giving 11 + 2 = 13 double bonds, plus 2 rings.

Wait, check carefully: the conjugated chain loses 2 double bonds to form the rings, but gains 2 rings. So total stays at 13.

**Conclude the hydrogen change**

Since total unsaturation is unchanged (13 to 13), the molecular formula stays the same. Both are in fact $\text{C}_{40}\text{H}_{56}$.

Therefore cyclisation forms two new C-C single bonds using the electrons from the pi bonds, with no gain or loss of hydrogen atoms per molecule.

options.A: Incorrect. Gaining 4 hydrogens would mean a large decrease in unsaturation, such as hydrogenating two double bonds. Here the number of double bonds plus rings stays constant, so no hydrogenation occurs.
options.B: Incorrect. Gaining 2 hydrogens would mean loss of one unit of unsaturation, for example loss of one double bond. Students may think ring formation saturates the ends, but one double bond is retained inside each new ring.
options.C: Correct. Lycopene cyclises at both ends to give beta-carotene. Two chain pi bonds are used to close two rings, so double bonds + rings = 13 in both molecules. With identical unsaturation, there is no change in hydrogen atoms.
options.D: Incorrect. Losing 2 hydrogens would mean an increase in unsaturation by one, such as forming an extra ring or double bond. Here forming 2 rings is exactly balanced by losing 2 chain double bonds, so net unsaturation does not increase.
